scenarios.requirement: Expired reservations are reclaimed after pre-dispatch and post-dispatch process failure, and concurrent callers cannot overspend or leak concurrency leases.
Database failure before dispatch releases safely; ambiguous failure after dispatch is never treated as an unused reservation.
Upstream disconnects and client disconnects cancel transport work, preserve the response-commit boundary, and settle one conservative outcome.
Configuration activation/rollback races and quota snapshots cannot mix revisions or mutable bucket generations.
Concurrent key initialization chooses one active key and rotation preserves sessions issued before rotation.
Unknown-kid refresh, JWKS rotation, bounded stale-key fallback, refresh singleflight, and database-shared replica cache work together.
Durable jobs are claimed exactly once across replicas and are recovered after a worker heartbeat failure.
Cancellation drains HTTP and worker roles, worker failure cancels HTTP, and a bounded drain timeout is surfaced.
DPoP, identity, session, quota, and identifier time boundaries fail closed or use explicit skew without state corruption during clock regression.
SIGKILL a released OCI process after a durable reservation but before dispatch, restart a worker, and prove the exact reservation is reclaimed without usage.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Requires process and database fault control against the release image; use an isolated environment and include before/after quota rows plus image digest.

scenarios.requirement: SIGKILL a released OCI process after an SSE first byte, restart worker/API replicas, and prove bounded conservative settlement with no permanently locked reservation.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Requires an isolated stream fixture, process fault control, a released image digest, and durable reservation/attempt evidence.

scenarios.requirement: Cut database connectivity before dispatch and during settlement, restore it, then prove fail-closed dispatch and bounded pending-usage reconciliation.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Requires network fault injection around PostgreSQL and must include request, upstream-observation, worker-reconciliation, and quota evidence.

scenarios.requirement: Send SIGTERM with in-flight non-stream and SSE work, prove the listener accepts no new work, and prove in-flight work ends within the configured drain bound.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Run against the release image with an explicit shutdown timeout and the deterministic load fixture.

scenarios.requirement: Drive a pre-response upstream disconnect, mid-SSE upstream disconnect, and downstream client cancellation through the released gateway, then prove one bounded terminal attempt and no retained reservation for each case.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Use the authenticated deterministic fixture control modes and preserve fixture observations, client results, attempts, usage provenance, and quota snapshots.

scenarios.requirement: Change configuration and gateway signing keys while requests span at least two API replicas and two workers, without mixed decisions or invalidating active sessions; issuer-JWKS rotation is proved separately by the shared-cache PostgreSQL scenario.
scenarios.evidence_notes: Requires a real load balancer, shared PostgreSQL, two API replicas, two workers, and exact release image digests.
